ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act of 10 October 1997 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG; SR 951.0), as amended by the UBO register provisions; Ordinance of 11 November 2015 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLO; SR 951.01); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), especially Article 627 and Articles 950-963; Commercial Register Ordinance of 17 October 2007 (HRegV; SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Protection of Public Symbols, Coats of Arms and Public Signs of 5 June 1931 (SR 232.21); FINMA Circular 2020/1 on money laundering and terrorist financing prevention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or other valid government-issued identity document of each UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in the country of origin or Swiss notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing State is a Contracting Party; consular legalization where the issuing State is not an Apostille Contracting Party; certified German, French, or Italian translation where the document is not issued in an official Swiss language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or current extract from the commercial register of each corporate UBO or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the country of organization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, accompanied by a sworn translation into an official Swiss language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract or certificate of no criminal record for each natural-person UBO and statutory officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss cantonal criminal record office or foreign competent judicial records authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where foreign; Swiss domestic extracts require no apostille; official translation into German, French, or Italian required where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed UBO declaration and PEP questionnaire, including a notarially attested signature specimen
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public or incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Swiss domestic notarization; no apostille required for internally executed documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or account-capacity pre-approval from the intended Swiss bank or FINMA-regulated financial intermediary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Swiss bank or FINMA-regulated asset manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct bank communication under internal AML policy; no apostille or consular legalization required for ordinary bank references

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of every UBO, director, signatory, and close associate against the United Nations Security Council sanctions and consolidated EU sanctions as given effect in Switzerland by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO); the Swiss domestic sanctions and embargo lists; the SECO Switzerland sanctions measures under Article 2 of the Federal Act on Material Sanctions; the U.S. Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list as a standard condition for USD clearing and correspondent banking relationships; and Interpol notices and domestic enforcement databases. Politically exposed persons, including foreign and domestic PEPs per FINMA Circular 2020/1 and FATF standards, trigger enhanced due diligence, written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior-management approval, and continuous monitoring. The AML/KYC file and all screening results must be retained for at least ten years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex / Swiss Central Business Index, https://www.zefix.ch) and SHAB (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt / Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce, https://www.shab.ch), administered with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be entered in the Latin alphabet and must not conflict with existing registered names. The commercial register accepts names in the official Swiss statutory languages of the canton of the registered office (German, French, Italian, and Rhaeto-Romanic) and, to the extent permitted by the competent register office, established foreign names rendered in Latin script. Foreign scripts such as Chinese, Cyrillic, or Arabic are not registered; a certified Latin-alphabet transliteration and, where necessary, an official translation into the applicable Swiss statutory language must accompany the incorporation application. The name must clearly identify the Aktiengesellschaft/SA legal form through the abbreviation AG or SA and must not mislead as to the company's purpose or territorial scope.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Genève / Zürich / Basel / Bern / Ticino and similar geographically protected canton or municipality names, where using them as a corporate name would indicate a false administrative, official, or governmental connection

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), Articles 620-763 governing the Stock Corporation (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411), Articles 16-24; Entry and Publication Ordinance (VPR, SR 221.411.1); Federal Act on the Amendment of Swiss Company Law of 1 January 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), Zentrastrasse 4, 6300 Zug, Switzerland; online filing via the central Swiss e-government platform ezeit.ch.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Application for Registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) accompanied by the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the Founding Report (Gründungsbericht) in accordance with Article 640 OR.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The mandatory minimum statutory share capital is CHF 100,000 (Art. 621 OR), of which at least 20% of each share's nominal value, and in aggregate no less than CHF 50,000, must be paid up in cash before registration (Art. 632 OR). Funds must be deposited into a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss-regulated bank and remain at the free disposal of the governing body; the bank releases the funds only upon presentation of the certificate of commercial register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CH_AG. The Board unanimously resolves: the entire statutory share capital of CHF 100,000 is fully subscribed and CHF 50,000 is paid up in cash through a blocked capital deposit account with a Swiss-regulated bank in the Canton of Zug; the registered office is adopted at the principal business premises in Baar, Canton of Zug, Switzerland; the corporate purpose is the manufacture and packaging of aseptic, barista-formula hydrolyzed oat milk; [Full Name] is appointed Chairman of the Board, and [Full Name] and [Full Name] are appointed Board members; [Full Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer; and the Chairman is authorized to execute and file the Commercial Register application with the Zug Commercial Register Office. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Authentication of Articles of Association and Founding Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary of the Canton of Zug (Notariat Zug) with prior name clearance through the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Zefix) database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a name clearance certificate from Zefix confirming that CH_AG does not conflict with an existing or deceptively similar business name; prepare the German-language Articles of Association (Statuten) and Founding Report (Gründungsbericht), including share classes, board powers, auditors, and purpose clauses; convene all incorporators before the Zug notary; verify identity using valid government-issued passports; execute the notarial deed of incorporation and obtain certified signatures.
required_dossiers: Government-issued passport or Swiss identity card of each incorporator
Draft Articles of Association in German
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate name is refused, propose up to three alternative names and re-execute a corrective notarial deed; the notary submits a revised application without restarting the incorporation procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Minimum Capital and Bank Blocked-Account Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-regulated bank in the Canton of Zug, e.g. Zuger Kantonalbank or a FINMA-licensed private bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked capital deposit account (Sperrkonto) in the provisional company name; deposit at least CHF 50,000 in cash from founders by SEPA or SWIFT TT; obtain a written blocking attestation (Bankenbestätigung) confirming that the full paid-up sum is irrevocably reserved and will be transferred to the company upon presentation of the commercial register certificate; complete standard bank due diligence forms including beneficial ownership declarations.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all transferring founders
Bank account opening and KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries source of funds, provide certified tax returns, salary slips, or asset evidence; if the deposit is rejected, redeploy the capital through a licensed Swiss payment institution holding client funds; repeat the blocking procedure within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) via the ezeit.ch portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the electronic or paper application for registration, enclosing the notarized deed, the Articles of Association, the Founding Report, the bank blocking attestation, and the signed board declaration on the exercise of legal representation; pay the registry invoice online; the Office verifies formal legality and statutory compliance, then orders entry; the registration is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and legal personality arises on that date.
required_dossiers: Board declaration of representation and authorization
Passport copies and power of attorney to the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice or reservation is raised, provide the omitted declaration within 10 calendar days; if the application is rejected, submit a corrected instrument to the Commercial Register Office and, if necessary, appeal to the Cantonal Appeal Commission for Administrative Affairs within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Registration, UID Assignment and Cantonal Tax Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and Tax Department of the Canton of Zug (Finanzdepartement / Kantonale Steuerverwaltung).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after commercial register entry, complete the online VAT (MWST) registration form on the ESTV portal, state the intended business activity under the Swiss NOGA code, and request the company UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer); register for cantonal income tax and capital tax prepayment; open the employer payroll account for withholding tax compliance; obtain export eligibility codes for EU/third-country shipment of UHT oat milk products.
required_dossiers: Composition of corporate purpose for VAT classification
Bank account details for tax purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID is not automatically generated, issue a manual application to the Swiss Federal Statistical Office; VAT underpayments are remedied by filing a revised quarterly return with statutory interest; oppose tax penalty orders by submission of a statement of facts within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Operating Authorization and HACCP Pre-Inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Health Department of Zug / Cantonal Chemist (Kantonschemiker) in cooperation with the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV); machine conformity reviewed by SECO.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the production facility as a food business establishment within the meaning of the Foodstuffs Ordinance (LGV, SR 817.02) and the Foodstuffs Act (LMG, SR 817.0); submit the self-monitoring concept, describing HACCP plans, allergen control, and the UHT aseptic process validation; arrange a pre-operational inspection of the manufacturing hall and packaging line; obtain the establishment operating approval for production and aseptic packaging of oat-based beverages destined for ambient-temperature distribution.
required_dossiers: UHT process and aseptic filling validation reports
Water hygiene certificate and plant layout plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If operating approval is withheld, remedy every listed deviation, submit a corrective action plan within 20 days, and request a follow-up inspection; if repeated non-conformity is found, negotiate a staged compliance schedule with the Cantonal Chemist before any commercial launch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Insurance, Fire Safety and Civil Defense Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Fire Inspectorate of Zug (Feuerpolizei), Cantonal Building Inspectorate, SUVA / approved accident insurance carrier, and the Employers' Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse Zug).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as an employer with the AHV compensation office; take out mandatory non-occupational and occupational accident insurance under the Accident Insurance Act (UVG) for all employees; submit the fire-protection plan, escape route schematic, and fire extinguisher layout to the fire inspectorate; obtain the structural load certificate for the UHT production hall, tank storage area, and packaging warehouse; appoint an internal safety delegate and issue a hazard assessment in line with ArGV 3.
required_dossiers: Fire protection and emergency evacuation plan
Workplace hazard assessment and safety delegate appointment order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If clearance is deferred, execute immediate remediation works, obtain a certified structural engineer endorsement, and resubmit the corrected file; in case of denial, appeal to the Cantonal Building Commission and request a technical mediation hearing within 10 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Health Department of Zug / Cantonal Chemist (Kantonschemiker), acting jointly with the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV) for food law, and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for machine and workplace safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Establishment Operating Approval for the Manufacture of Aseptic UHT Plant-Based Beverages (Betriebsbewilligung des Lebensmittelunternehmens, Arts. 54-64 LGV), supplemented by the Canton of Zug industrial plant building permit and the UHT line machinery conformity certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) with the Cantonal Environment Office of Zug (Amt für Umwelt, AfU) and the municipal wastewater authority of Baar.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Preliminary Environmental Assessment (Vorentscheid) is mandatory before plant construction; a full EIA Report (Umweltverträglichkeitsbericht) is required only where production exceeds 20,000 tonnes/year of finished product or 500 hl/day of beverage output under Annex 1 items 40.1 and 40.3 of the EIA Ordinance (UVP-V); below-threshold plants complete a simplified screening with the cantonal environment office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must meet the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) limits: pH 6.5-9.5, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 400 mg/L, total phosphorus ≤ 10 mg/L; process exhaust gases from the UHT line must comply with Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) Annex 3 values for volatile organic compounds < 150 mg C/m³ and odour thresholds in the neighborhood; beverage processing sludges and packaging waste must be recovered or incinerated in accordance with the Waste Ordinance (VVEA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire resistance and evacuation certification from the Cantonal Fire Inspectorate in line with VKF/NKGS fire norms; structural load approval for the UHT process hall, silo tanks, and palletized packaging racks from the Cantonal Building Inspectorate; occupational health and safety clearance under ArGV 3 and the Swiss Labour Law, including 45-hour weekly limits, rest intervals, ergonomic workstations, mandatory accident insurance coverage through SUVA, and designated emergency assembly points.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni ATC) – VAT Division and corporate income tax units. Official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity intending to carry out taxable activities in Switzerland (including B2B/B2C supplies of goods or services) must apply for a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and VAT registration via the ESTV eVAT portal. The registration application must identify the foreign entity, its legal form, beneficial owners, and the proposed Swiss business activity. Non-established taxable persons must ordinarily appoint a fiscal representative resident in Switzerland to receive notifications and settle VAT liabilities (Art. 67 VAT Act). Where the annual worldwide turnover from taxable activities exceeds CHF 100,000, registration is mandatory for taxable supplies made or carried out in Switzerland; where turnover is below this threshold, voluntary registration is available. The UID number, once issued, serves as the Swiss VAT identification number for invoicing and customs purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a US-style check-the-box system; an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is always a separate taxable legal entity for direct taxes and cannot elect pass-through treatment. For Swiss VAT, a group of closely affiliated legal entities may elect to be treated as a single taxable person under Art. 12 VAT Act (VAT group election), with at least a 50% capital interest and uniform business purpose. For corporate income tax purposes, a Swiss AG may elect to form a tax consolidation group with its 80%-owned domestic subsidiaries (Art. 61(3) of the Swiss Direct Federal Tax Act) for offsetting profits and losses, provided the election is made under cantonal and federal tax law. No elective hybrid mismatch mechanism is available; Swiss tax law applies the OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable activities (excluding VAT itself, exempt supplies and certain incidental real estate transactions). A foreign supplier carrying out taxable supplies in Switzerland is required to register once this threshold is exceeded based on worldwide business turnover; voluntary registration applies below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland imposes no real-time government fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing obligation comparable to the Italian Sistema di Interscambio. Electronic invoices are accepted provided the authenticity of origin and integrity of content are guaranteed by recognised controls (e.g., Swiss QR-bill, ZUGFeRD/eBill or EDI interchange). The Swiss VAT Act prescribes required invoice content, but does not mandate a specific electronic clearing mechanism. Swiss QR-invoices are mandatory only for paper-based payment slips related to Swiss bank payments; they are not a VAT clearance device.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods are zero-rated when the goods are physically exported from Switzerland into a foreign territory and the supplier or the recipient (if supplier-instigated transport) provides satisfactory proof of export within legally defined time limits (Art. 23 VAT Act). The supply of services related to exported goods or services rendered directly to recipients abroad may also be zero-rated where the recipient is not established in Switzerland and benefits from the supply abroad. The taxable person must retain documentary proof showing the goods left Swiss customs territory, the commercial nature of the transaction, and the consideration paid. For UHT oat milk packaging operations under ISIC 1050, export zero-rating applies when finished aseptic packaged oat milk products are sold to a foreign buyer and physically dispatched from Switzerland to the destination market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss export customs declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / export declaration processed through the Swiss Customs eRecipients system)
Commercial invoice, packing list, and transport contract evidencing the sale and dispatch of the goods
Bill of Lading / CMR consignment note / airway bill showing the goods left Swiss customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/TT wire evidence substantiating receipt of consideration where required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may audit export zero-rating cases by requesting full documentary proof. Missing or false export documentation triggers immediate retrospective reassessment at the standard VAT rate, together with default interest. In cases of intentional tax evasion or misleading documentation, the responsible persons are subject to administrative fines under the Swiss VAT Act and the Federal Act on Administrative Penal Law, and fraudulent claims can lead to criminal prosecution. Documents must be retained for at least ten years; a failure to substantiate the export transaction prohibits the refund of input VAT associated with the exported goods and creates a direct VAT clawback liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) - Schweizerische Nationalbank, in coordination with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) and the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) for international financial market policy and sanctions-related oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains unrestricted current and capital account convertibility. The CHF is fully freely convertible, and there are no exchange control approval requirements for cross-border payments, dividend remittances, or capital repatriation. Dividend and profit remittances by a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft are subject to a 35% Swiss federal withholding tax absent treaty relief, but no SNB authorization or FX license is required. Payments to non-resident shareholders are permissible in any currency. Sanctions screening is mandatory but does not restrict currency convertibility as such.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no prescribed repatriation timeline. Export receipts in EUR, USD, or other currencies may be retained, converted, or transferred freely. The only obligations are ordinary commercial record-keeping, VAT/accounting treatment under Swiss law, and compliance with Swiss sanctions and anti-money-laundering reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account / Wealth Management Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as the principal corporate banking venue. Swiss-licensed fintech banks and service providers may support limited onboarding and payment functionality, but they do not substitute for a tier-1 commercial bank in respect of full SIX SIC clearing, commercial LC capacity, and large cross-border trade settlements. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not viable as primary operating accounts for a Swiss AG, as accepting deposits or conducting payment business without a Swiss banking licence would contravene Article 1 of the Swiss Banking Act and FINMA circulars.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In general, for a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft, the ultimate beneficial owner and the authorised signatory(ies) must appear physically before the relationship manager or a delegated notary/bank agent for identity verification and the KYC interview. Remote onboarding is available only where the bank accepts a qualified Swiss electronic ID and the corporate structure is deemed low-risk. For this cross-border oat milk manufacturing entity, physical presence is the de facto mandate at most tier-1 Swiss banks, especially for non-resident UBO structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unidentified ultimate beneficial owner due to layered non-resident shareholding or nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered political structure chart; notarised share register; Swiss-certified copies of passports of all UBOs; corporate registry extracts from home jurisdictions; declarations of source of wealth and source of funds; group organizational chart certified by board resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of economic substance at the registered office or production facility
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed office lease agreement; site inspection photographs of the UHT plant; proof of active employees with Swiss social security registrations; utility and telecommunications invoices; production machinery invoices; Swiss VAT registration; management accounts reflecting operational activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade payments to or from counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial invoices and pro-forma invoices; bill of lading or airway bill; end-user certificates; sanctions screening reports for each counterparty; know-your-supplier documentation; standard industry letters confirming absence of dual-use or embargoed goods; documentary evidence of beneficial ownership of counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unexplained inbound capital injection for plant equipment and working capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised board minutes approving capital increase or contribution; executed shareholder subscription agreement; bank account funding trail from disclosed shareholder account; shareholder loan agreement with commercial interest rate and repayment schedule; audited financial statements of the contributing shareholder; source-of-funds confirmation of the origin of the remitted funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex shareholder structure involving trusts, foundations, or offshore entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trust deed or foundation charter; registrar / trustee declaration identifying settlor and beneficiary; certificate of incumbency from registered agent; UBO register or statutory declaration under Swiss AML rules; legal opinion from Swiss counsel certifying every natural person in the ownership chain; consolidated group structure chart with ownership percentages.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be routed through SWIFT MT103 or MT210 messages to the Swiss bank account held at a SIX SIC/RTGS participant. For capital increases, the remittance information should include purpose code 'CAPC' or 'A300' together with reference to the notarised capital increase resolution and the Swiss Commercial Register filing. The Swiss bank will require documentary proof of origin of funds and a completed AML form; no SNB prior approval is required. Verification on the receiving side includes matching the remitter with the shareholder register and confirming the injection has been booked in the commercial register within the statutory timeline.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for UHT plant materials and oat milk packaging should use SWIFT MT103 remittances for full prepayment, open account, or documentary collection; for larger capital equipment tranches, a commercial letter of credit (irrevocable, confirmed where appropriate) is the recommended clearing rail. Payment instructions must state the correct SWIFT purpose code, submit the underlying invoice, packing list, transport document and, where relevant, the LC terms. For EUR and USD payments, Swiss clearing can be executed via the corresponding nostro accounts with SIX SIC or SIX Interbank Clearing governing CHF leg; cross-currency payments settle via correspondent institutions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX spot contracts and outright forward forwards up to standard ISDA maturities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exposures involving inconvertible or restricted currencies, settled in CHF or USD
Cross-currency swaps for long dated machinery financing and term liabilities
Vanilla FX options (calls and puts) including zero-cost collars and participating forwards for USD/EUR/CHF exposure
Treasury FX swap lines for reversible short-term liquidity swaps between CHF and major currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT declaration and balance adjustment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 April of the following calendar year for annual filers; quarterly filers must reconcile by the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to CHF 8,000; default interest at 5% p.a.; criminal sanction in cases of gross negligence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (acting for the Federal Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 30 June of the year following the calendar tax year; cantonal extensions may extend to 30 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing default interest of 4–5% p.a.; penalty surcharges up to 30% of tax due; compulsory tax assessment; criminal fines for willful omission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage statement for AHV/AVS social insurance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January of the year following the wage reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late reporting interest; recovery of unpaid contributions; administrative fine up to CHF 30,000; debt enforcement under SchKG/LP

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit under CO Art. 727 if the company exceeds at least two of the three thresholds (CHF 20m balance sheet total, CHF 40m annual revenue, 200 full-time employees) for two consecutive years; limited statutory audit under CO Art. 727a if it exceeds at least two of CHF 4m balance sheet total, CHF 8m revenue, 20 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO Arts. 957–963) and Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS is an acceptable alternative for a Swiss AG not listed

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law has no general public UBO annual filing. The company must keep its share register (Aktienbuch) current and, where applicable, an internal register of beneficial owners in accordance with the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act. Updates are event-driven (share transfers) and must be made without delay; an internal annual board confirmation is a best-practice compliance control.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss federal corporate income tax rate is 8.5% on net assessable profit (DBG Art. 68). The aggregate federal, cantonal and communal burden is higher: effective combined rates range from approximately 11.9% (Canton Zug, the reference canton for the entity) to approximately 15.0% (Canton Zurich), because cantonal and communal profit taxes are added to the federal layer and are deductible in the federal assessment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: qualifying dividends and capital gains from holdings of at least 10% or with a market value of at least CHF 1,000,000 are effectively tax-exempt at federal and cantonal levels. Patent Box/IP deduction: up to 90% of qualifying income from Swiss-developed patents and comparable IP can be carved out, reducing the effective federal burden on qualifying IP income to approximately 1.0%. R&D super deduction: up to 150% of qualifying Swiss research and development labour costs. Notional Interest Deduction (NID): mandatory deduction on excess shareholder equity of Swiss principal companies since 1 January 2020. Cantonal capital-tax relief may apply through reduced assessed equity schedules.
